timeline.body: The Strait of Hormuz narrows to just 24 miles between Iran and Oman — roughly one-fifth of the world's daily oil supply passes through it, giving Iran a chokepoint over the global economy whenever tensions escalate.

The CIA and MI6 overthrew Iran's democratically elected Prime Minister Mohammad Mossadegh after he nationalized the country's oil industry, reinstalling the Shah as an authoritarian Western client ruler.

The United States supplied Iran with a nuclear research reactor and weapons-grade enriched uranium under the Atoms for Peace program — the foundation of the very nuclear capability Washington would spend decades trying to destroy.
The Iranian Revolution toppled the US-backed Shah and replaced a monarchy with an Islamic republic under Ayatollah Khomeini, severing Iran's alliance with both the United States and Israel overnight.

Iraq invaded Iran with quiet American encouragement, beginning an eight-year war that killed half a million people while Saudi Arabia and the Gulf states bankrolled Saddam Hussein's military to contain the Islamic Revolution next door.

Israel bombed Iraq's Osirak nuclear reactor near Baghdad and declared the Begin Doctrine: no hostile state in the region would be allowed to approach nuclear weapons capability — a principle Israel has enforced by force ever since.

The US Navy reflagged Kuwaiti oil tankers and escorted them through the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran-Iraq War, establishing the precedent that American military power would guarantee Gulf oil flows against Iranian disruption.

USS Vincennes shot down Iran Air Flight 655 over the Persian Gulf, killing all 290 civilians aboard — the US never formally apologized, and the incident remains a defining grievance in Iranian memory of American presence in the Gulf.

An Iranian dissident group revealed that Iran had been secretly building uranium enrichment facilities at Natanz and a heavy-water reactor at Arak, setting off two decades of escalating nuclear confrontation.
The US invasion of Iraq destroyed Iran's greatest military rival and inadvertently extended Iranian influence across a contiguous arc of allied territory from Tehran through Baghdad to Beirut.

The Stuxnet computer worm, jointly built by the US and Israel, destroyed roughly a thousand Iranian centrifuges at Natanz — the first cyberweapon known to have physically sabotaged another nation's infrastructure.

Israeli operatives assassinated at least four Iranian nuclear scientists using magnetic bombs attached to their cars on Tehran streets, part of a covert campaign to slow enrichment progress by eliminating the people who understood it.

Iran and six world powers signed the JCPOA, trading strict limits on enrichment for sanctions relief — the most significant diplomatic opening between Washington and Tehran since before the revolution.

Saudi Arabia severed diplomatic ties with Iran after protesters stormed the Saudi embassy in Tehran following Riyadh's execution of Shia cleric Nimr al-Nimr, formalizing a rivalry that had been escalating through proxy wars in Yemen, Syria, and Iraq.
Trump unilaterally withdrew the United States from the JCPOA and reimposed maximum-pressure sanctions, prompting Iran to resume enrichment and steadily approach weapons-grade uranium levels.
A US drone strike at Baghdad airport killed General Qasem Soleimani, the architect of Iran's entire regional proxy network, pushing the two countries to the brink of open war.

The Abraham Accords normalized relations between Israel and the UAE, Bahrain, Sudan, and Morocco — understood in Tehran as the formation of an anti-Iranian military alignment along its southern flank.
China brokered a surprise restoration of Saudi-Iranian diplomatic ties, briefly suggesting the Gulf's defining rivalry might be managed through Beijing rather than Washington.
Decades of proxy conflict between Iran and Israel escalated into direct military exchanges for the first time, with both sides launching strikes on each other's territory.
Israeli and American forces struck Iranian nuclear facilities, crossing a threshold that successive US administrations had debated for over a decade but never acted on.

iran-us-israel-war.label: Iran-US-Israel war: Gulf states weigh military entry, Hormuz blockade tightens

timeline.body: Congress passed the Antideficiency Act, making it illegal for federal agencies to spend money not yet appropriated — the obscure fiscal law that would eventually become the mechanism for shutting down the entire US government.

Hijackers began diverting US commercial flights to Cuba, launching a two-decade epidemic of skyjackings that forced governments worldwide to invent the concept of screening passengers before they board an aircraft.

After more than 130 hijackings worldwide, the FAA mandated screening of all passengers and carry-on bags — then handed the job to the airlines, who outsourced it to the cheapest private security contractors they could find.

The United States is one of the only democracies where a failure to pass a budget causes the government to stop functioning — most parliamentary systems have automatic continuing resolutions that prevent shutdowns entirely.

President Reagan fired 11,345 striking air traffic controllers and imposed a lifetime federal employment ban, establishing the precedent that essential transportation workers who refuse to work face career-ending consequences.

House Speaker Newt Gingrich forced two government shutdowns totaling 26 days over budget disputes with President Clinton, transforming the funding lapse from a bureaucratic glitch into a recurring partisan weapon.

Nineteen hijackers passed through airport checkpoints staffed by private screeners earning around six dollars an hour, boarded four commercial aircraft, and killed 2,977 people — exposing American airport security as a low-bid façade.

Two months after the attacks, Congress federalized airport screening by creating the Transportation Security Administration, adding roughly 60,000 federal employees in the largest expansion of the government workforce in decades.

The Homeland Security Act merged 22 separate federal agencies into the Department of Homeland Security — the most sweeping US government reorganization since the Department of Defense was created in 1947.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement began operations by absorbing the enforcement arms of both the Immigration and Naturalization Service and US Customs, giving a single new agency jurisdiction over immigration raids, deportations, and trade investigations.

Congress deliberately placed TSA screeners outside the normal civil service system, stripping them of the collective bargaining rights, pay scales, and workplace protections that other federal employees receive.

TSA screeners voted to join the American Federation of Government Employees after years of organizing, but their bargaining rights remained far more restricted than those of any other unionized federal workforce.

A 16-day government shutdown furloughed 800,000 federal workers, but TSA screeners were classified as excepted — legally required to show up and screen passengers with no guarantee of when their next paycheck would arrive.
A 35-day shutdown over border wall funding became the longest in US history; TSA agents worked without pay as sickout rates at major airports doubled and security wait times stretched to hours.

The record shutdown ended only after the air traffic controllers union warned of an emerging safety crisis and TSA absence rates hit 10 percent, demonstrating that unpaid aviation workers effectively hold a veto over prolonged shutdowns.
TSA secured its first significant pay adjustment in two decades, raising the average screener salary from roughly $36,000 to $47,000 — still below the federal employee average for comparable work.

The Trump administration expanded ICE enforcement operations into domestic airport terminals, with agents detaining travelers at gates and check-in areas — extending immigration policing well beyond traditional border zones and ports of entry.

tsa-ice-dhs-shutdown.label: TSA workers unpaid in second shutdown as ICE militarizes airports
